First, we complete the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{2}-12x+40 \\  & =({x}^{2}-2\cdot 6x+{6}^{2})-{6}^{2}+40 \\  & =(x-6)^{2}-36+40 \\  & =(x-6)^{2}+4\end{aligned}
$$

    

To find the inverse of a function, we follow these steps:

**Step 1:** Replace $f(x)$ with $y$:

$$
y=(x-6)^{2}+4
$$

**Step 2:** Swap $x$ and $y$:

$$
x=(y-6)^{2}+4
$$

**Step 3:** Solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =(y-6)^{2}+4 \\ x-4 & =(y-6)^{2} \\ \sqrt{x-4} & =y-6 \\ \sqrt{x-4}+6 & =y\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we selected the positive square root because if $x\ge 6$ is the domain of $f,$ then the range of the inverse is ${f}^{-1}\ge 6.$

**Step 4:** Replace $y$ with ${f}^{-1}(x)$:

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x-4}+6
$$
